correctness.rationale: Each setwise invariant face is a union of whole edge-orbits. The vertical two-edge orbits intersect at a middle vertex and cannot occur; a horizontal pair and a middle singleton each contribute a factor of −1 to the signed orbit sum, with an overall minus coming from reduced chain degree. Tracking possible incoming rows as sets and accepting zero outgoing occupancy at the last column correctly tests extendibility without counting multiple completing tilings. The seven states, terminal vector, A^6 b=b and odd-power starting values (0,−1,1) were independently reconstructed. Direct tiling and orbit-face enumeration for n=1 through 5 also gives these signed sums periodically. The primary theorem supplies the degree and rank for n≥2 and contractibility at n=1. On barycentric chains the involution preserves the order of each stabilized chain, so the quotient chain complex is the coinvariant complex; over Q, averaging is exact and identifies coinvariant and invariant homology. Thus t₂=t₃=−1, t₄=0 and the quotient has its first positive rank, one, at n=4. The argument does not decide integral quotient homology.
